title: Three small faults in this branch's own changes: dead keys after Go to Folder from a Smart Folder's filter field, Relevance chosen again reruns the search, and quick clicks swallowed after a double-click on a message button
problem:
Found by the review of the whole branch (20 Nov), in which one reviewer read all the improvements together through one lens and a second reviewer tried to refute each finding against the code. Nothing was run in that review: every finding was traced by reading. [goto-folder-from-smart-folder-filter-field-dead-keyboard] Go to Folder confirmed with Return from the filter field of an open Smart Folder leaves the keyboard on a field that is no longer drawn: every key is dead until a click. The finder's scenario: Steps (not run, traced in the code): 1) a Smart Folder saved with a Nushell filter is in the sidebar, and the window's own filter bar is closed. 2) Click the Smart Folder: its search runs and the filter bar opens with its filter. 3) Click in the filter field (leave the text as it is). 4) Press Cmd+Shift+G (Ctrl+L on Linux and Windows), type a folder or keep the one offered, press Return. What happens: the window goes to the folder, which ends the Smart Folder's search and puts the window's own setup back, so the filter bar goes away. The dialog then closes and the kit hands the keyboard back to what had it when the dialog opened: the filter field, which is not drawn. Keys are now dispatched from the window's root only, so the arrow keys, typing, Cmd+F, Cmd+Shift+G, Escape and the Mac menu bar's commands do nothing until something is clicked (or Tab is pressed). Expected: the files have the keyboard, as they do when the same Smart Folder is left with Cmd+[ from its filter field (tests/controls.rs:4155-4160) or with the dialog's Go button (dialogs.rs:726-729). Neither rescue reaches this case: replace_filter's own hand-off needs the field to have the keyboard at that moment, and the dialog has it; keyboard_lost acts only when the thing that lost the keyboard was inside the browser, and here it was the dialog, drawn outside it. With the dialog's exit animation the window is blurred first, so when the keyboard lands on the undrawn field no focus-lost event fires at all. The same end state follows when a second launch or `fff gui PATH` (open_request) or `fff show` (show_results) navigates the window while any dialog opened from that filter field is up. Before 60df179 a Smart Folder's filter bar stayed open after navigation, so the field was still there. The code path: src/finder/dialogs.rs:672-678 go_to_folder -> :30-35 focus_before_dialog keeps the keyboard in a focused field (`!window.has_focused_input(cx)` is false), so the kit records the filter field as the handle to return to (gpui-component-0.8.1 src/root.rs:383). Return: gpui-base-0.8.1 src/dialog.rs:586-600 Confirm -> on_ok (dialogs.rs:716-718) -> submit_go_to :747-770 -> src/finder/mod.rs:1269-1275 navigate -> :2095-2104 end_search -> src/finder/filter.rs:380-407 leave_smart_folder -> :283-302 replace_filter(before.filter, before.filter_open): filter_open = false and the filter empty, so filter_bar_open() is false; the hand-off at :298-301 needs `field.is_focused(window)`, false while the dialog's field has the keyboard. The bar is drawn only while open (mod.rs:4415-4417). The dialog then closes through request_confirm(true) -> gpui-component src/root.rs:455-485 defer_close_dialog -> `window.focus(&handle, cx)` (:482) for the filter field's handle. src/finder/mod.rs:2596-2615 keyboard_lost returns because the nearest drawn ancestor of what went is in the dialog layer, not in the browser (:2607), and gpui-pre-0.3.10 src/window.rs:3537-3545 fires focus-lost only when the frame before had a focus path. Keys then go to the root node only: gpui-pre-0.3.10 src/window.rs:6507-6515. The second reviewer, who tried to refute it and confirmed it, corrects the scenario: As the finder wrote it, with these precisions.

1. The filter text must be as the Smart Folder set it. An edited filter counts as changed by hand (filter.rs:398), keeps its bar and its field, and nothing goes dead. This makes the flow narrow: a click in the field without a lasting edit, then Go to Folder by key, then Return.

2. Only Return ends this way. The Go button gives the files the keyboard itself (dialogs.rs:726-729).

3. Tab probably does not rescue, contrary to the finder's aside. The kit binds Tab in the "Root" context, which sits on a div below node 0 of the dispatch tree, and keys are dispatched on node 0 alone. Not verified by running.

4. Any press inside the browser does rescue: keyboard_stays (mod.rs:2631) gives the files the keyboard when the browser does not contain what has it, and a click on a row calls focus_files. Cmd+Q and Cmd+N still work.

5. The variant with an external navigation (open_request, show_results) while a dialog opened from that field is up holds by the same code, including when that dialog is then closed with Escape or its close button, but it is rarer still. Their evidence: Traced by reading; nothing was run (rules). No guard found.

1. The dialog remembers the filter field. src/finder/dialogs.rs:30-35 `self.end_rename(window, cx); if !window.has_focused_input(cx) { self.focus_files(window, cx); }`: with the caret in the filter field the keyboard stays there (the kit registers a focused input as it renders, input/state.rs:371-393). gpui-component-0.8.1 src/root.rs:383 `let mut previous_focused_handle = window.focused(cx).map(|h| h.downgrade());`. The key reaches go_to_folder from that field: src/actions.rs:173 and :314 bind it in the Finder context, and no kit input binding takes those keys.

2. Return takes the bar away under the dialog. dialogs.rs:716-718 on_ok -> submit_go_to (:747-770) -> src/finder/mod.rs:1269-1272 navigate -> end_search (:2095-2098) -> src/finder/filter.rs:380-404 leave_smart_folder, which calls `self.replace_filter(before.filter, before.filter_open, window, cx)` when the filter and bar are as the Smart Folder set them. filter.rs:298-301: `let field = self.filter_input.read(cx).focus_handle(cx); if field.is_focused(window) && !self.filter_bar_open() { self.focus_files(window, cx); }`. The dialog's own field has the keyboard, so there is no hand-off. The bar is drawn only while open: mod.rs:4415-4417 `.when(self.filter_bar_open(), ...)`, and the field is drawn nowhere else (grep filter_input).

3. The kit gives the keyboard to the undrawn field. gpui-base-0.8.1 src/dialog.rs:586-598 Confirm -> `request_confirm(true, window, cx)` -> gpui-component src/dialog/dialog.rs:756-764 -> src/root.rs:455-485: `window.blur(cx)` (:443) while the dialog animates out, then after 0.25 s `window.focus(&handle, cx)` (:482) for the filter field's handle. Window::focus does not check that the handle is drawn (gpui-pre-0.3.10 src/window.rs:2417-2427). Only the Go button calls focus_files itself (dialogs.rs:726-729).

4. Neither rescue fires. mod.rs:2600-2609: `let Some(nearest) = window.focus_lost_restore_target(cx) else { return; }; if self.renaming.is_some() || !self.focus.contains(&nearest, window) { return; }`. The dialog layer is drawn by the kit outside the browser (root.rs:770). gpui-pre src/window.rs:3540 fires focus-lost only `if !previous_focus_path.is_empty() && current_focus_path.is_empty()`: after the blur the path is already empty when the keyboard lands on the undrawn field, so no event fires. With reduce motion the dialog is removed at once, its field's handle is dropped and nothing of its path is still drawn, so the net returns at the first line; the later focus again fires nothing. No other focus-lost listener exists in src, the kit or the workspace.

5. Keys are dead. gpui-pre src/window.rs:6507-6514 falls back to `root_node_id()`. Every binding but Quit, Settings and New Window is in the Finder or files context, and the handlers are on the browser's div (mod.rs:4262 onward). Only Quit and New Window have global handlers (src/lib.rs:134, 140).

History: at a6b81fc end_search (mod.rs:1774-1780) did not call leave_smart_folder, so the bar stayed after navigation: new with 60df179.

Tests: tests/controls.rs:4155-4160 leaves the Smart Folder with Cmd+[ while the filter field itself has the keyboard. The Go to Folder tests (controls.rs:3331-3470) start with the keyboard in the files.

Records: not in any done record or in final-pass-notes.md. focus-lost-recovery's record says dialogs are unchanged and that its probes covered the files, the search field and a tree put away under a dialog ("since focus_before_dialog moves it to the files first"); the filter field is not among them. [relevance-rechosen-reruns-search] Choosing Relevance again in a search's Sort menu flips a direction it doesn't have and runs a cut search again. The finder's scenario: Results shown 3; a folder with a.log, b.log, c.log, d.log; search `*.log` (status bar `3+ items`, sort Relevance). Open Sort and View Options (or the empty-space menu's Sort By) and click the checked item Relevance.
What happens: `result_sort` becomes Relevance/descending, so the menu now shows Descending checked beside two disabled direction items. Because the answer on screen says a sort may choose its items, the search is also started again: spinner, and the rows are replaced by another run. On a broad search that run can list other items among ties, and a selected row that drops out loses its selection.
What should happen: nothing. Relevance has no direction (the manual: "Both are disabled for Relevance"). The review of sorted-search-results already made the checked Ascending/Descending items do nothing for this same reason; the checked key was missed. The code path: src/finder/toolbar.rs:775-788 lists Relevance while searching and calls `set_sort(key)` on click. src/finder/mod.rs:3169-3175 flips `ascending` whenever the chosen key is the current one; mod.rs:3182-3185 stores it and calls `result_sort_changed`. src/finder/mod.rs:2352-2357 runs the search again unless the answer on screen has `sort_chooses` false. crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:1029 sets `sort_chooses` on the answer of an unsorted search whose list was cut; engine.rs:883 drops a Relevance sort, so the new run is the same plain search. src/finder/toolbar.rs:792-806 draws the two check marks. Upstream's `set_sort` only stored the order, so the flip was harmless before 26ab60c. Their evidence: Traced by reading the snapshot at 7e8df53; no guard, reset or early return stops it.

1. src/finder/toolbar.rs:775-787 lists Relevance while searching. `.checked(sort.key == key)` only draws the mark; the item's `on_click` calls `this.set_sort(key, cx)`. The kit runs the handler of any item that is not disabled (gpui-component-0.8.1 src/menu/popup_menu.rs:228-240 `is_clickable`, 870-886 `activate`).
2. src/finder/mod.rs:3170-3175: `let current = self.sort_order(); let order = if current.key == key { SortOrder { key, ascending: !current.ascending } }`. There is no exception for Relevance.
3. mod.rs:3182-3185: `if self.is_searching() { let read_for_results = self.result_reads(); self.result_sort = order; self.result_sort_changed(read_for_results, cx);`
4. mod.rs:2352-2357: `let answer = self.search_stats.as_ref().filter(|_| !self.searching); if answer.is_some_and(|stats| !stats.sort_chooses) { self.read_more_for_results(had, cx); } else { self.run_search(false, cx); }`
5. The plain answer of a cut `*.log` has the flag set. crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:883 drops a Relevance sort (`req.sort.filter(|order| order.key != SortKey::Relevance)`), 1029 sets `sort_chooses: truncated && sort_can_choose(&hits, &words, loose)`, and 2112-2113 with 2433-2436 make that true for a search with no words. The existing test a_sort_chooses_among_every_match_not_among_the_ones_listed depends on it: its first click on Size could not list other items otherwise.
6. `start_search` sets `self.searching = !quiet` at once (mod.rs:2214) and the answer replaces the rows (2285 `this.results = rows`). `new_search` is false, so the selection is remapped by path (1844) and a selected row that is gone loses it.
7. The only guard of this kind is in `set_ascending` (3204: `if self.result_sort.ascending != ascending`).
8. toolbar.rs:792-804 draws Ascending `.checked(sort.ascending)` and Descending `.checked(!sort.ascending)`, both `.disabled(sort.key == SortKey::Relevance)`, so the mark moves to the disabled Descending.

Upstream's set_sort (66c919b, src/finder/mod.rs:2133-2158) flipped the direction too but only stored it, so the second search came with 26ab60c.

No test covers it: tests/controls.rs:1100 and 1201 choose Relevance only from another key, and 1045-1051 pins only `set_ascending`. Both asserts of the finder's test idea would fail today (`searching` is true as soon as set_sort returns; `ascending` is false).

Not in any done record or in final-pass-notes.md. The record of sorted-search-results says of Relevance "On any other list it takes no search", which this case contradicts.

One part I did not run: that another run can list other items. It rests on fff-search cutting ties in no fixed order (fff-search-0.11.0 src/score.rs:581 `select_nth_unstable_by`; engine.rs:2630-2640), which final-pass-notes.md records as still true for broad searches.
proposal: Reproduce each fault first with a test that fails on the trunk. Then fix it. The finder's suggested fixes, as starting points and not checked plans: [goto-folder-from-smart-folder-filter-field-dead-keyboard] A net at draw time, beside keyboard_lost: at the top of Finder's render, if `!self.filter_bar_open()` and the filter field's handle `is_focused(window)`, call focus_files and ask for one more frame with `window.defer(cx, |window, _| window.refresh())`. It covers the external navigations too. Narrower alternative, three lines: in focus_before_dialog, give the files the keyboard first when the focused field is the filter field and `smart_folder_setup.is_some()` (the bar can go with that search). [relevance-rechosen-reruns-search] In `Finder::set_sort`, return early when `key == SortKey::Relevance` and the current key is Relevance (or never flip `ascending` for Relevance).
original_test_plan: The finder's test ideas: [goto-folder-from-smart-folder-filter-field-dead-keyboard] tests/controls.rs, with atlas_folders(&fx) as in the test at :4137: ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.add_smart_folder(filtered, cx)); ui.click(("smart", 0usize)); ui.click("filter-input"); ui.press(&cmd("shift-g")); ui.type_text(&fx.path("Projects").display().to_string()); ui.press("enter"); assert!(!ui.dialog_open()); assert!(!ui.exists("filter-input")); assert!(ui.files_focused()) (fails today); ui.press("down"); assert_eq!(ui.selected().len(), 1). [relevance-rechosen-reruns-search] In a_sort_chooses_among_every_match_not_among_the_ones_listed, right after `set_query("*.log")` with the limit at 3: `view.update(cx, |f, cx| { f.set_sort(SortKey::Relevance, cx); assert!(!f.search_in_flight_for_test()); assert!(f.current_sort().ascending); })`. Both asserts fail today. Why the existing tests miss it: [goto-folder-from-smart-folder-filter-field-dead-keyboard] tests/controls.rs:4137-4175 (the_keyboard_stays_in_the_window_when_a_smart_folder_takes_the_filter_bar_away) leaves the Smart Folder with a key that acts while the filter field itself has the keyboard (Cmd+[ and Cmd+]). The Go to Folder tests (tests/controls.rs:3331-3470) all start with the keyboard in the files. The focus-lost-recovery tests cover parts of the browser that go away and say dialogs are unchanged; no test closes a dialog whose return target has gone meanwhile. [relevance-rechosen-reruns-search] tests/controls.rs:1044-1051 (in a_sort_chooses_among_every_match_not_among_the_ones_listed) pins only `set_ascending` with the direction already had. tests/controls.rs:1099-1101 clicks Relevance only when coming from Size. No test chooses the key that is already current.
original_risks: This is a fix late in the branch: keep it to the fault. Every test on the trunk has to keep passing, and the improvements involved (focus-lost-recovery, smart-folder-save-and-leaks, sorted-search-results) have tests that pin the behaviour around the fault: read their done records in /home/user/polish-tools/done/ before changing the functions they changed.

verifier.claim_check: A second reviewer traced the same path and confirmed it; neither ran anything. Reproduce before changing anything; if a test shows the fault is not there, write the closed record with the evidence and return skipped.

orchestrator_notes: This fault is in a change that is itself unreleased, so it gets no entry in CHANGELOG.md. In the commit message write the paragraph as `Changelog: none (fixes a fault in an unreleased change).` instead of `Changelog (Fixed): ...`, and in the done record set changelog_kind to "Fixed" and begin `changelog` with "(No entry: a fault in an unreleased change.)" followed by one sentence on what was wrong. The full findings, with the second reviewer's evidence line by line, are in /home/user/polish-tools/review/*.md and *.json (search for the finding ids in brackets). The review read the branch at 7e8df53; other changes have landed since, so read the functions as they are now. A third fault of the same kind, found by the reviewer of 'stray-double-click-opens-file' (its done record, first item under 'Found, not fixed'): the guard for the buttons under the file area's message (`message_button_clicked`, from 'empty-state-messages') stops every quick click on the results after a double-click on Search This Computer until a click the system counts as first, so a double-click on the result under the pointer opens nothing until the mouse rests or moves. Their pointer: clear the flag at the first left press on the file area, whatever its count; the press after the stopped one is then left alone once more by the `Presses` rule unless the guard records its press as left alone too. Decide whether `Presses` now makes the guard unnecessary for the result under the button (it does not cover 'the other button' case, which tests/controls.rs a_double_click_on_a_button_under_no_results_doesnt_press_the_next_one pins). Three faults, three tests, one commit; if one of them turns out not to be there, say so and fix the others.
